title: "5.8 Monitoring plan"
order: 8

## What is monitored

Adjudication is monitored as two things: the model's PD, and the decisions the policy layer
makes from it. Each new cohort of applicants is compared with the development sample and,
once outcomes are known, measured against the development performance. The thresholds are
the same policy constants D4 uses (`wiki/facts/policy.py`), printed here by name.

| Metric | Population | Threshold | Frequency | Action on breach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PD-zone mix: PSI over the three zones | new applicants vs the held-out development applicants | below {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} stable; {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} to {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}} watch; above {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}} act | every cohort | Watch: find the inputs that moved, the score first. Act: review with the validator. |
| Decision mix: PSI over Approve / Refer / Decline | new applicants vs the held-out development applicants | same | every cohort | As above; a shift with a stable zone mix points at the rules, not the model. |
| Rule-hit rate, each of the seven rules | new applicants | a rule with no hits in a cohort; any rule's hit share moving by more than {{< var monitoring.rule_hit_move >}} of its development share | every cohort | No hits: report to the policy owner as an untested control. A large move: check the input's source before the rule. |
| Share of Declines carrying a knockout | new applicants | reported, not thresholded | every cohort | Read the PD gates against it. |
| Observed / predicted default rate, by PD zone | booked loans with outcomes | ratio outside {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}} to {{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}, on at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} defaults | when outcomes mature | Below the floor: record and watch. At or above it: count toward trigger 3. |
| Observed default rate, by decision | booked loans with outcomes | Approve above Refer, or Refer above Decline | when outcomes mature | The decisions no longer rank: review with the validator. |
| AUC and lift, all applicants | the cohort's applicants with outcomes | below the gates, {{< var adj.gate_auc >}} and {{< var adj.gate_lift >}}× | when outcomes mature | Gate breach: redevelopment ([5.9](gate.qmd)). |
| AUC and lift, booked only | the cohort's booked loans with outcomes | AUC falling more than {{< var adj.auc_ci_half >}} from development; lift below {{< var adj.gate_lift >}}× | when outcomes mature | Review with the validator; weigh gating on the booked (finding 1). |
| Zone cutoffs at a retrain | the retrained model | either cutoff moving by more than {{< var adj.sens.step >}} of its committed value | every retrain | The mix was held and the risk accepted moved: the policy owner signs off the new cutoffs before they are used ([5.4](assumptions.qmd#adj-thresholds-are-quantiles)). |

The booked rows are the control for finding 1; the zone calibration row for findings 3 and 6; the
rule-hit row for finding 2; the cutoff row for the assumption that a fixed mix is the right
policy. As in D4, the fall that triggers review on the booked AUC is the half-width of the
all-applicant interval: the booked sample is smaller and its own interval wider, so the
threshold is deliberately the stricter one.

## Rule hits and dead rules {#adj-rule-hits}

A policy rule that never fires is a control that cannot be shown to work. The rule-hit row
above is the detection: every cohort's hit count for each of the seven rules, read from the
reason strings `decide` writes. At development, two rules already have no hits — the leverage
knockout and the large-request override — on all {{< var adj.n_applicants >}} applicants
(finding 2). They are flagged from the first cohort, and stay flagged until the policy owner
restates or removes them. A rule that *stops* firing after firing at development is a
stronger signal: an input whose definition or source has changed.

Hit counts are rule hits, not decisions: an override can fire on a file that a knockout then
declines ([5.3](methodology.qmd#adj-policy-layer)).

| AUC | {{< var adj.auc >}} | held-out applicants |
| Lift, riskiest {{< var adj.lift_top_share >}} | {{< var adj.lift >}}× | held-out applicants |

| Lift, booked only | {{< var adj.pop.booked.lift >}}× | held-out booked applicants |
| Decision mix, Approve / Refer / Decline | {{< var adj.mix.Approve >}} / {{< var adj.mix.Refer >}} / {{< var adj.mix.Decline >}} | held-out applicants |

| Declines carrying a knockout | {{< var adj.decline.knockout_share >}} | held-out Declines |
| Zone cutoffs, `t_low` / `t_high` | {{< var adj.t_low >}} / {{< var adj.t_high >}} | quantiles over all applicants |

| `weak_score` override | {{< var adj.rule.weak_score.share >}} | held-out applicants |

| PD zone | Observed / predicted | Defaults behind it | Population |
|---|---|---|---|
| Approve | {{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.ratio >}} | {{< var adj.zone.booked.Approve.defaults >}} | held-out booked applicants |
| Refer | {{< var adj.zone.booked.Refer.ratio >}} | {{< var adj.zone.booked.Refer.defaults >}} | held-out booked applicants |
| Decline | {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.ratio >}} | {{< var adj.zone.booked.Decline.defaults >}} | held-out booked applicants |

The Approve and Decline zones are already outside the tolerance at development, on enough
defaults to count: findings 3 and 6, each with its own control. The first cohorts with matured outcomes
are read against trigger 3 for those two zones before any other.

## Redevelopment triggers {#adj-redevelopment-triggers}

Any one of these starts a redevelopment, with the validator informed:

1. The all-applicant AUC or lift on a cohort with outcomes falls below its gate.
2. PD-zone or decision-mix PSI above {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}}.
3. A zone's observed / predicted ratio outside the tolerance in two consecutive cohorts, each
   with at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} defaults behind that zone. Below
   that count a breach is recorded and watched, not acted on. The Approve and Decline zones
   already breach at development (findings 3 and 6).
4. A change to any input's definition or source — including any change to the scorecard,
   which is an input ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd#what-a-scorecard-change-forces)).

Two further events go to the credit policy owner rather than to redevelopment: a change to
any policy value, after which [5.5](performance.qmd) and [5.6](sensitivity.qmd) are re-run;
and a rule with no hits (above).

A redevelopment is also where the open findings and observations of [5.7](limitations.qmd)
are acted on, and where three questions this chapter leaves open are answered: whether the
zones should sit on the scorecard's PD instead of the LightGBM's
([5.3](methodology.qmd#alternative-considered-pd-zones-on-the-scorecards-pd)); how the model
performs refitted on reduced inputs, with the score recomputed from them
([5.6](sensitivity.qmd#reduced-input-refits-not-run)); and whether a calibrated PD changes
the zones (finding 3). Every redevelopment re-runs [5.5](performance.qmd) and
[5.6](sensitivity.qmd) and passes both gates.

## What is automated today

This plan is documented, not yet automated. The platform has one cohort of applicants, so
there is no new population to compare. What runs today is the development side:
`python verify.py` recomputes the held-out AUC and lift against its own copies of the gates
([5.9](gate.qmd)), and recomputes every fact on these pages — every rule's hit count included
— from the committed model, policy and data on every run ([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd)).
A rule with no hits is visible in the generated rule table on every build, but nothing yet
fails on it.
